title: Black pole sticker (northern coast)
description: The black sticker on utility poles is very common, visible from afar, and indicates the whole coast north of Lima.

title: Gen 3 in Tacna
description: Gen 3 is becoming increasingly rare in Peru. Combined with desert, mountainous landscape, it most likely means the far south, in the Tacna region.

title: Arequipa football chick party emblem
description: Each Peruvian political party has its own emblem. One of the easiest to remember is the number-9 football chick, found in Arequipa.

title: Small camera around Cusco
description: In Peru, the small camera is found exclusively in the immediate surroundings of Cusco.

title: Overhanging roofs of northern Peru
description: In northern Peru, roofs tend to overhang the walls by a wide margin. This is never seen south of Lima, and usually indicates areas well north of it.

title: Yellow warning stickers with the voltage (Ica)
description: In Ica, the yellow 'Peligro Riesgo Eléctrico' stickers carry the voltage (kV) just under the warning text — this exact design, with no other text.

title: Yellow warning with separate kV/code stickers (San Martín, Amazonas)
description: In San Martín and Amazonas, under the yellow warning there is a separate sticker with the voltage and a code (letters = nearby city), usually with a third sticker. Also by the border in Loreto around Yurimaguas, where the code starts with YU.

title: Long warning stickers, 'Peligro Alta/Media Tensión' (Loreto, Iquitos)
description: On the Gen 3 road to Iquitos and in the city, warnings are unreadable but longer than usual, often with a green-white-red 'RST' sticker above. In Iquitos almost every pole says 'Peligro Alta Tensión' or 'Peligro Media Tensión' (rarely in San Martín and Ucayali).

title: Black warning stickers (northern coast)
description: The most common warning style in the northern half of the country: from the city of Lima north to the Ecuador border in all coastal regions and Cajamarca (also possible in Cusco).

title: White barcode stickers, barcode first (Tumbes, Piura)
description: In Tumbes and Piura the white sticker is mainly a barcode, with small numbers under it that are usually unreadable. Rarely seen in other regions.

title: White barcode stickers with big numbers (Ica)
description: Ica barcode stickers look like the Tumbes/Piura ones, but the numbers below the barcode are much bigger and usually partly readable. Rarely in Ucayali or Loreto.

title: White stickers with numbers above the barcode (Lima)
description: In Lima Region and Lima Province the numbers are in the centre of the sticker, even bigger than in Ica, with the barcode below them — or no barcode at all.

title: 6 vertical digits, black on yellow (Tumbes, Piura)
description: Six black digits on yellow, written vertically: common in Tumbes and Piura, also found in Lambayeque, Cajamarca and Tacna. Usually paired with other regional markings.

title: 7 vertical digits, black on yellow (Cajamarca, La Libertad, Áncash)
description: Seven black digits on yellow, vertical: most common in Cajamarca, La Libertad and Áncash, rarely Piura, Lambayeque and Tacna (always borderless in Tacna). Sometimes two letters replace the first two digits. If the code does not start with 0, the first digit gives the region: 2 or 4 Áncash, 3 Cajamarca, 5 La Libertad.

title: 8 vertical digits, black on yellow (La Libertad)
description: Eight black digits on yellow, vertical: La Libertad (one each found in Cajamarca and Áncash).

title: 9 vertical digits, black on yellow (Lambayeque)
description: Nine black digits on yellow, vertical: rare, but found in Lambayeque and rarely La Libertad or Áncash. Sometimes two letters replace the first two digits.

title: 4 vertical digits, black on yellow (Áncash)
description: Four black digits on a yellow background can sometimes be spotted in Áncash.

title: 5 rotated vertical digits (Apurímac, Cusco, Madre de Dios)
description: Five (sometimes six) rotated digits written vertically are only found in Apurímac, Cusco and Madre de Dios, often with the yellow warning; in Cusco sometimes with another rotated marking, in Madre de Dios usually with an XX-00 marking starting with PM.

title: XXX-000 code, black on yellow (Cajamarca, La Libertad, Áncash)
description: Three letters and three digits, horizontal, usually paired with 7–9 vertical digits or a 2-letter 4-digit marking. Found in Cajamarca, La Libertad and Áncash, rarely Lambayeque. The letters refer to a nearby city (CAJ-000 = around Cajamarca).

title: XX0000 code, black on yellow (Cajamarca, La Libertad, Áncash)
description: Two letters and four digits, horizontal, usually paired with 5, 7 or 8 vertical digits; common in Cajamarca, La Libertad and Áncash, sometimes Lambayeque. The letters refer to a nearby city: CJ Cajamarca, HI Trujillo, EN Chiclayo, CH Chimbote.

title: Very long 0XX00000 + …DP… codes (Junín, Pasco, Huánuco)
description: Two codes almost always paired, so long you cannot read them without moving around the pole: the short one usually starts with 4, the long one has the letters DP in the middle. Most common in Junín, Pasco and Huánuco, sometimes Ayacucho, Huancavelica or Cusco. The two letters after the 4 refer to the place (see map).

title: XX-00 code, black on yellow (Madre de Dios, Apurímac)
description: Two letters and two digits, horizontal: Madre de Dios and Apurímac, rarely Cusco and Arequipa, likely paired with 5 rotated vertical digits. In Madre de Dios it always starts with PM (Puerto Maldonado); in Apurímac TA, AN or CP; in Cusco CH or TI; in Arequipa SE.

title: A0000 code, black on yellow (Tumbes, Piura)
description: One letter and four digits, horizontal (X0000 or X-0000): only in Tumbes and Piura, and it always starts with an A.

title: 0000-0000 code, black on yellow (Piura, Sullana)
description: Eight digits in two groups of four, horizontal: only in Piura, especially common in Sullana (where 000-0000 also occurs). Usually you won't see all eight digits.

title: 000-00 code, black on yellow (Piura, Tumbes)
description: Five digits, horizontal (000-00): not very common, found in Piura and Tumbes, usually with another vertical sticker.

title: 'Woolen' poles with the region name
description: Poles wrapped in a textured protective layer, marked FITEL MTC, a thin red stripe, the region name (full or shortened) and 4m. The region name tells you where you are. Most common in Puno, Tacna, Moquegua and Junín on the guide's map.

title: Road code 1-5-00 (Desaguadero)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. Codes 1-5-01 start slightly south of Desaguadero and run north into the town, up to about 1-5-56.

title: Road code 1-1-000 (Desaguadero–Mazocruz)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-1-000 (three-digit end) runs from Desaguadero to Mazocruz, up to about 1-1-900.

title: Road code 1-2-000 (Mazocruz–Hualtire)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-2-000 runs west from Mazocruz towards Hualtire, up to about 1-2-780.

title: Road code 1-3-0000 inland (Moquegua–Hualtire)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. A second 1-3-0000 section runs from Moquegua north-east to the Hualtire area (the other 1-3 section follows the coast from Tacna to Ilo).

title: Road code 1-4-000 (Moquegua–Ilo)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-4-000 runs between Moquegua and Ilo, up to about 1-4-800.

title: Road code 1-1-0000 (Mazocruz–Tarata)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-1-0000 runs from Mazocruz to Tarata, up to about 1-1-1300; around the Puno/Tacna border codes are near 1-1-0689 (lower = Puno, higher = Tacna).

title: Road code 1-2-0000 (Tarata–Tacna)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-2-0000 runs from Tarata to Tacna, up to about 1-2-0800.

title: Road code 1-3-0000 on the coast (Tacna–Ilo)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-3-0000 runs from Tacna along the coast to Ilo, up to about 1-3-1550 — you should see the ocean on most of it.

title: Road code 1-4-0000 (Ilo–Mollendo)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. 1-4-0000 runs along the coast from Ilo to Mollendo, up to about 1-4-1550 (near the Moquegua/Arequipa border codes are around 1-4-718).

title: Road code 1-9-0000 (west of Arequipa)
description: Poles on some southern roads carry a black code 1-0-0000 / 1-0-000 / 1-0-00: always starting with 1, the second digit gives the road section, the last group counts poles from 01/001/0001 along it. Found on concrete poles with blue IDS / BOLIVIACOM text, or on 'woolen' poles with a yellow stripe. Since the 2025 coverage, the road west of Arequipa has 1-9-0000 codes, from about 1-9-0513 at the junction of roads 30 and 1S near Estación San José up to 1-9-0993 in Arequipa.

title: 3-digit road codes between the two Yuras (Arequipa)
description: On the road between the two places called Yura, north of Arequipa, poles carry three-digit codes going up from 001 in southern Yura to 345 in northern Yura (2025 coverage).

title: 'e' marking with a region code
description: A lowercase 'e' marking (sometimes blue), most often in Piura and Ica but found in many regions. The first two digits of the code below it give the region: 21 Piura, 14 Lambayeque, 13 La Libertad, 15 Amazonas, 01/02 Lima, 12 Junín (also Lima Region near Huánuco), 11 Ica, 04 Arequipa, 19 Moquegua, 24 Tacna.

title: '5m' written at the bottom of poles (north)
description: Poles with '5m' written near the bottom are only found in the north of the country, especially Tumbes, Piura and La Libertad.

title: Ensa sticker (Lambayeque)
description: Blue text on a white sticker with a black border, or a plain company-style marking: a good clue for Lambayeque.

title: Blue-on-white divided markings (Tacna, Moquegua)
description: Blue-on-white divided markings (sometimes inverted, white on blue), in many formats but always the same look: very useful for Tacna and Moquegua.

title: Red or blue on white vertical digits (Arequipa)
description: Four to six red-on-white or blue-on-white vertical digits: very useful for Arequipa (red ones rarely in Lima Region).

title: Black on white 6 vertical digits (Tumbes, Piura)
description: Six (or seven) black digits on white, vertical: not very common, observed in Tumbes and Piura.

title: Puno pole stickers
description: Puno poles usually carry a yellow warning (sometimes with a red-bordered triangle), an RST sticker, a black-on-white sticker with three rows of characters, and a blue (sometimes red) band. That black-on-white sticker is found only in Puno.

title: Black on white 5 horizontal digits (Ucayali, Pucallpa)
description: In Pucallpa poles often carry a combination of four stickers; the black-on-white sticker with five digits is also found elsewhere in Ucayali.

title: White kV stickers (Lambayeque, Cajamarca)
description: White voltage stickers, whose letters refer to the nearby city (JAE = Jaén): Lambayeque and Cajamarca.

title: Black kV stickers (Lima)
description: Black voltage information stickers are found in the Lima Region.

title: Red on white XX-00 stickers (Lima Region)
description: Red-on-white XX-00 stickers: rare, found only in the Lima Region.

title: LDS pole marking (Lima)
description: LDS poles are unique to Lima Region and Lima Province, much more common in Lima Province and in the southern half of Lima.

title: MEGALUZ pole marking (San Martín, Loreto)
description: MEGALUZ poles are found only in San Martín and Loreto.

title: PdN pole marking (Piura)
description: PdN markings are most common in Piura, also in Tumbes, Lambayeque and Áncash.

title: COMOL pole marking (Arequipa)
description: Most COMOL poles are in Arequipa; rarely in Cusco and Madre de Dios.

title: EDELNOR / EDEL pole marking (Lima)
description: EDELNOR poles are found in Lima Region and Lima Province, more likely in the northern half of Lima (unlike LDS, in the south).

title: ENOSA pole marking (Piura)
description: ENOSA is by far most common in Piura; Tumbes also has some.

title: ICASAC pole marking (Ica)
description: ICASAC is most common in Ica, also in Ayacucho and Huancavelica (Castrovirreyna and Huaytará provinces).

title: PYE pole marking (San Martín)
description: PYE markings are rarer, but present in San Martín (most common on the map), Cajamarca and Amazonas.

title: HHSAC pole marking (Ica)
description: HHSAC is rarer, but a good tip for Ica; also found in Huancavelica.

title: INCH pole marking (Áncash)
description: INCH is rare, but found only in Áncash.

title: TPCH poles (Lambayeque)
description: TPCH poles have a distinctive design, with markings often on a blue-painted background. Most common in Lambayeque, also Tumbes, Cajamarca, Amazonas, Piura and La Libertad.

title: PNSA pole marking (north-west)
description: PNSA markings are most common in Piura, Lambayeque, Cajamarca and La Libertad, also Tumbes and Áncash. Don't confuse with PSA or PASA.

title: IPS pole marking (Piura)
description: IPS markings are most common in Piura on the guide's map. Don't confuse with IDS.

title: PASA pole marking (Arequipa)
description: PASA markings are most common in Arequipa on the guide's map, rarer across the south.

title: ELC / ELCTO / ELCTRO pole marking (Junín, Huánuco)
description: ELC / ELCTO / ELCTRO markings are most common in Junín and Huánuco on the guide's map, also Pasco, Áncash, Huancavelica, Ayacucho and Ica.

title: IDS pole marking (Tacna)
description: IDS markings are most common in Tacna on the guide's map (also Puno and elsewhere in the south). Don't confuse with IPS.

title: EPC pole marking (Lima)
description: EPC markings are most common in the Lima Region on the guide's map.

title: ELORSA pole marking (Cajamarca, San Martín)
description: ELORSA markings are most common in Cajamarca and San Martín on the guide's map; in Loreto found in Gen 4 coverage.

title: BITEL pole marking on road 28A (Ica–Ayacucho)
description: BITEL is always written horizontally (unlike FITEL). It is absent from most southern coastal regions except Ica, and very common on road 28A from around Humay (Ica) to the city of Ayacucho.

title: FDC / FADICO pole marking (north-west)
description: FDC / FADICO markings are most common in Tumbes, Piura, Lambayeque, La Libertad and Áncash on the guide's map.

title: PRONATEL pole marking (Arequipa, San Martín, Huánuco)
description: PRONATEL markings are most common in Arequipa, San Martín and Huánuco on the guide's map.

title: Claro pole marking (Piura)
description: Claro markings (red, a logo or a plain company marking), usually with a code ending in P: most common in Piura on the guide's map.

title: SEAL pole marking (Arequipa)
description: SEAL markings seem regional to Arequipa (few observations — use with caution).

title: ENEL pole marking (Lima Province)
description: ENEL markings seem regional to Lima Province (few observations — use with caution).

title: PPP pole marking (Tumbes, Piura)
description: PPP markings seem regional to Tumbes and Piura (few observations — use with caution).

title: FASK pole marking (Ica)
description: FASK markings seem regional to Ica (few observations — use with caution).

title: PRETAC pole marking (Tacna)
description: PRETAC markings seem regional to Tacna (few observations — use with caution).

title: CREMOL pole marking (Cajamarca)
description: CREMOL markings seem regional to Cajamarca (few observations — use with caution).

title: TMX pole marking (Madre de Dios)
description: TMX markings seem regional to Madre de Dios (few observations — use with caution).

title: 'Four rectangles' poletop without support (Cajamarca)
description: A poletop with three horizontal bars and one vertical, looking like four rectangles, with no support: most common in Cajamarca on the guide's map, rarer across the north and centre.

title: 'Four rectangles' poletop with support (Cusco, Apurímac, Puno)
description: The same four-rectangle poletop, but with a support forming a triangle or trapezoid with the first bar: most common in Cusco, Apurímac and Puno, rarer in Madre de Dios and Arequipa.

title: Trapezoid pole support (Cusco)
description: In the south, especially Cusco but also Madre de Dios and Huancavelica, a support mounted on the side of the pole forms a trapezoid with the poletop (not when mounted around the pole).

title: Inverted triangle poletop (Cusco, Madre de Dios)
description: The inverted triangle poletop is found in Cusco and Madre de Dios.

title: Light and dark blue painted pole bases (Callao)
description: In Callao poles often have a light blue / dark blue painted section at the bottom.

title: Three-sticker combination (Tarapoto)
description: Common in the city of Tarapoto: top sticker C-00, middle sticker seven characters ending in a letter, bottom sticker seven digits.

title: RST, grey warning and white kV stickers (Chiclayo)
description: A sticker combination you may meet in the city of Chiclayo: green-white-orange RST sticker, greyish warning sticker and white kV sticker.

title: Black vertical digits and white 5-digit stickers (Arequipa city)
description: In the city of Arequipa some poles carry vertical black digits (usually six, sometimes three or four after a T or A — T codes also exist in other cities), and white stickers with five digits.

title: White stickers on poles (Iquitos)
description: These white stickers can be found on poles in the city of Iquitos.

title: White reflector stickers on wooden poles (road 1S, Arequipa coast)
description: White reflector stickers on wooden poles exist in many places, but with the ocean to the south-west you are most probably on this section of road 1S along the Arequipa coast.

title: Bright yellow reflector stickers (Marcona)
description: On this white road near Marcona in southern Ica, wooden poles carry bright yellow reflector stickers.

title: Indented poles (Arequipa)
description: Indented poles resembling Chilean ones can sometimes be found in Arequipa (not confirmed — use with caution).

title: 'AT' warning stickers (Puno)
description: Yellow warning stickers with the letters 'AT' seem to be found only in Puno (not confirmed — use with caution).

title: Diagonal-striped pole markings (Ica)
description: Diagonal-striped markings similar to Taiwan's, seen in Ica (not confirmed — use with caution).
